# dsh-plugin-verispring

A three-role session architecture plugin (leader — scout — executor) with a bundled local
knowledge

graph (manon). The main session keeps the premium model but never reads the codebase
itself; the hea

vy work runs on DeepSeek Flash and the main-session context stays clean — which
cuts premium model A
PI costs substantially.
*leader dispatches → scout maps the repo and answers facts → executor builds → receipt back to the l
r dispatches → scout maps the repo and answers facts → executor builds → receipt back to the leader*
中文 | English
## What it does
### Three-role division, enforced by dispatch discipline
The leader plans, dispatches and reviews. A resident scout owns the repository map and touches code

read-only; executors write code and run commands. The role comes from the dispatch itself, an
execut

or dispatch is refused while no scout is reachable, and executors start only once the map
exists and

is fresh. Briefs go straight to the child and results come back as settlement receipts,
so the main

session is never polluted by raw exploration. The manon graph is scout-owned — leaders
and executor

s never invoke it directly; they ask the scout. Running executors per leader session are
capped (def
ault 8), so a dispatch fan-out cannot turn into a crowd.
### Global work-spec supply

The global work spec has a single production source: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. The plugin supplies it
t

hrough the root-scope dynamic system section `caseos:global-work-spec`, reading the full text at
eve

ry prompt assembly for leader, scout and executor sessions alike — including `send_message`
continua

tions and cold recovery; a subagent brief cannot opt out. When a task touches the specialized
specs
the source references, those specs are read in full at the paths the source gives.
If the source is missing, blank, or unreadable, new subagent dispatches and every tool call from an

existing subagent are refused with `spec-source-missing` and written to the monitor; the leader's
or
dinary tools are unaffected. Once the source is restored the next round proceeds — nothing is cached
inary tools are unaffected. Once the source is restored the next round proceeds — nothing is cached.
### Model division that saves money

The main session runs the premium model (Claude Opus 5.5 by default); scouts and executors default
t

o DeepSeek Flash. The route is enforced at runtime per role — a provider/model passed on the
dispatc

h call is ignored — so the cheap route cannot be slipped past. Both agent routes are picked in
the p
lugin panel; the main session uses DSH's native model picker.
### Cache cost defense
Tool definitions and regular system sections are frozen per session, so new copy shipped in a releas

e
never rewrites the prompt prefix of a session already running; the global spec section is an
inten

tional dynamic exception and is re-read every round. Compaction is per role: the main session at
40%

of its window, subagents at 60%. A main session that has been idle for 55 minutes with more than
50

K tokens is compacted once — flattening the large cache write that follows an expired cache TTL.
The
accepted cost: oversized tool results stay in context until a compaction summarises them.
### Memory and host guards

Heap thresholds warn and prune the plugin's own indexes long before the cliff; an out-of-process
wat

chdog keeps sampling while the host event loop is stuck; an oversized whole-file read is refused
wit

h a segmented-read hint; and the leader can release finished subagents to hand memory back. The
host
is never killed behind your back — the hard threshold only records a restart prompt.
### Secret hygiene

Credential files (`manon.env`, `verispring.env`, project `.env*`) cannot be read or echoed, and
whol
e-environment dumps are refused. Key values never reach a session log.
### Observability

Role drift, gate denials, dispatches, releases and memory events all land in
`~/.dsh/verispring-moni
tor.jsonl`, so audits no longer require decompressing session logs.
### Operational switches
Capabilities including the memory guard and scout division have `CASEOS_*` switches, so they can be
disabled individually without uninstalling: e.g. `CASEOS_MEM_GUARD=0` disables the memory guard and

its watchdog, and `CASEOS_SCOUT=0` drops the scout part of the division clause. Global work-spec
sup
ply and its fail-closed gate have no such bypass.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The desktop app enables HMR, so an install through the plugin manager applies immediately — no
resta

rt needed. Already-running sessions keep their current tree; new sessions and dispatches pick up
the

new one. Only setups with HMR disabled (headless/SDK/ACP) need a restart. To update, uninstall
and
reinstall the same spec.

**Prerequisites** — the profile needs the agent preset registry and a `preset-standard` entry
(deskt

op and web bundles ship them); `~/.dsh/specs/子代理派遣规范.md` and
`~/.dsh/specs/代码写作规范.md` must exist (th

e gates keep denying with directions otherwise);
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` must exist, be readable and n

on-blank (subagent dispatches and subagent tool
calls are refused otherwise); the `verispring` chann

el must serve the leader model and a
`deepseek-flash` entry that declares
`reasoningEfforts` and `co

mpat.forceAdaptiveThinking`. manon is bundled and optional: it bootstraps a
Python venv on first run

(one-time network, python3 ≥3.11), with keys in `~/.dsh/manon.env` and
`~/.dsh/verispring.env`.
> **Exclusive discounts**: contact the package author — **20% off Claude, 50% off DeepSeek Flash**;
> WeChat: `jinyong0716`.
## Test
`npm test` runs the gate behavior suites plus the smoke check (`npm run smoke`). Mock suites cannot

prove the host really loads the gates, so after a dsh upgrade run `npm run smoke` on its own: it
che

cks the manifest, the syntax and the plugin entry, and with `DSH_BIN` and `DSH_SMOKE_PROFILE` set
it
adds the official `--dump-config` composition check against an isolated profile.
